deliverables: 12 months of operations from August 2026 to July 2027
Periodic independent audits of treasury fund use in February 2027 and August 2027
Oversight metrics including balances, conversion rates, transaction hashes, and treasury repayment hashes
request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund 12 months of Eternl operations, maintenance, and improvements, including frontend and backend maintenance/development, infrastructure, support, administration, and audits/oversight metrics.

claims.claim: Eternl is a non-custodial Cardano light wallet for web, browser extension, Android, and iOS used for payments, staking, governance, and DApp interaction.
The proposal requests ₳2,350,000 at about $0.1787 per Ada to cover around $420,000 of annual operating cost for 12 months.
The budget allocates 55% to frontend, 25% to backend, 5% to support, 13% to admin, and 2% to audits.
The proposal funds 6.0 FTE distributed across 10 contributors at $70,000 per FTE.
Eternl plans to introduce Pro plans priced at $96 per year for personal users and $360 per year for companies, and says about 5,500 users would fully cover the $420,000 annual cost.
The proposer says Eternl has about 100,000 browser extension installs and about 30,000 installs across Android and iOS.
The proposer says 10-18% of Cardano mainnet transactions are conducted via Eternl.
The proposer commits to convert up to $420,000 worth of Ada into stablecoins in a public company wallet and return any Ada above that amount to the treasury.
The proposal says independent audits of treasury fund use will be performed by a party unaffiliated with Tastenkunst GmbH or Eternl in February 2027 and August 2027.
The proposer says every paid Pro plan will be recorded on-chain with metadata and that Pro plan earnings reports plus repayment or donation transaction hashes will be published.

summary: The document requests ₳2,350,000 for 12 months of Eternl operations administered by Tastenkunst GmbH, with a stated path toward paid-plan sustainability, future repayment mechanics, and audit/oversight commitments, but many adoption and impact claims are asserted without evidence in the anchor text.
